title: Construct a four-call compensated two-image pair (no new κ)
body:
Construct a complete two-input interface `(x,y) -> (F_f x, F_f^-1 y)` for both retained two-image prefixes at every positive tensor width. It uses four paid rank-one C calls, eleven scalar ADDs and no clean logical array. The original word has 42 primitive address applications; the phase-repaired word has 138. The inverse uses the same program with two bank swaps. Norm and inverse norm are three, giving condition number nine uniformly in width.

The construction uses the source's order-four free inverse polynomial and source-restoring elementary shears. The second output is explicitly transformed, so its volume compensates the first; it is not returned dirty state or an independently credited Gaussian job. This is a constructive changed contract beyond PR4991, not a kappa improvement or a paid-call saving. The denominator15, missing Gaussian consumer, and remaining native precision/storage/routing bill are explicit.

Validation: registered normal/optimized replays pass. A separate dense oracle builds the intended F and obtains its inverse by Gaussian elimination, without using the generated inverse polynomial or shear schedule. All288 independent input columns across the two variants are checked (width1 over Q(i), width2 over F17), with both inverse orders, an additional width3 dirty fixture, exact literal invoices and semantic controls. Source-history/committed-byte and whitespace checks pass. No native supplier, selected cold replay, Lean or complete five-in-fourteen proof is claimed.

Credit lee-phys/PR4688 for the original prefix and inverse polynomial, Yiyang/PR4710 for the phase repair, Dugongue/PR4743 for arbitrary-input triangular ports, and Jacob Alan Sussman/PR4628 with eumemic and Swapnil Jain for the source engine and framework. The block/shear identity is standard. Original sources and notices are unchanged.

Canonical continuation: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19138901. Exact assignment, scope, source pins, overlap coverage and remaining questions are in the package. Prepared by Cinna Davis with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Apache-2.0. No independent human or proof-assistant verification claimed.
